title: Privacy friendlier Cloudflare DoH resolver
body:
**Is your feature request related to privacy?**
Yes

**Is there a patch available for this feature somewhere?**
Yes, it's an edit request

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Mozilla partenered with Cloudflare for their DoH resolver and they have a resolver (https://mozilla.cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query) which limits logged data and data retention, opposed to the 1.1.1.1
Can it be used instead the current 1.1.1.1 if DoH flag value is set to Cloudflare?

[Source article](https://www.ghacks.net/2018/04/02/configure-dns-over-https-in-firefox/)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
any
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
This is the special agreement: https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/commitment-to-privacy/privacy-policy/firefox/

The privacy policy for 1.1.1.1 is instead: https://developers.cloudflare.com/1.1.1.1/commitment-to-privacy/privacy-policy/privacy-policy/

In both cases you can see:
> All information collected by Cloudflare, no matter whether such information is part of Cloudflare’s temporary or permanent logs, will be cleansed of any personally identifiable data (including your IP addresses). Additionally information that is stored as part of Cloudflare’s permanent logs will be further anonymized.

An important question: is the main difference between the two that Cloudflare is sharing this DNS data with Mozilla? It is not stated explicitly that it is not the case.

The only difference I can see is that the data used for Cloudflare permanent logs contains less fields, but I would like to know if there is an agreement between Cloudflare and Mozilla about sharing such data first.

**Edit:** I think the wording gives away the relationship between Cloudflare and Mozilla:
> Any data Cloudflare handles as a result of its resolver for Firefox is as a date [sic] processor acting pursuant to Firefox’s data processing instructions.

(date is a typo, should be data)

This means Firefox (they mean Mozilla?) is the data controller second GDPR parlance, thus it also has access to the data.

If this is the case, then I deny this request: we do not need to share the data with two companies instead of one.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
Yes, they mix up Mozilla and Firefox (the browser).
You're right, form those lines seems both have access to it, even if the data collected in the permanent logs is less, as you said too.
Feel free to close the issue. Thank you for your time.

comments.author: Participant 2
Participant 3
comments.body:
Isn't this a matter of Cloudflare + APNIC vs Cloudflare + Mozilla? 
The Mozilla version does not contain any references of APNIC, so it is just about Firefox's telemetry, if any.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: @Madis0 the Mozilla version means Mozilla + Cloudflare + APNIC
